# Empirical Evaluation and Clinical Validation

## Study Design, Biomedical Cohorts, and Synthetic Ground-Truth Regimes

We evaluate the nine architectures defined in Chapter 2 across twelve multi-view benchmarks: six real biomedical and clinical cohorts (`ADNI-MCI`, `MultiOmics` [TCGA-BRCA], `TCGA-KIRC`, `Heart`, `Diabetes`, and `mfeat`) and six synthetic generative regimes with known ground-truth latent coordinates $\mathbf{U}^*$ and feature supports $\mathbf{V}_m^*$ (@tbl-benchmark-cohorts). Every model is evaluated across three independent 70/30 stratified or random train/test splits (seeds $42, 43, 44$) across three `nsa_flow` quantile sparsity levels ($q \in \{\text{None}, 0.5, 0.8\}$, totaling $1,215$ cross-validation fits), supplemented by a $1,214$-configuration hyperparameter sweep on `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$). To prevent data leakage, all feature standardization (`StandardScaler`), column completeness filtering ($\ge 98\%$), and demographic covariate adjustments (Frisch–Waugh–Lovell residualization [@frisch1933partial; @lovell1963seasonal] of age, biological sex, and education inside `ADNI-MCI`) are fitted strictly within each training split and applied out-of-sample to the held-out test split.

In `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$) [@mueller2005; @jack2008alzheimer; @ADNI], Views 0–2 capture $382$ regional structural MRI features derived via the ANTs longitudinal and cross-sectional cortical thickness and Desikan–Killiany–Tourville (DKT) parcellation pipelines [@avants2008symmetric; @avants2011reproducible; @tustison2014large; @desikan2006automated; @klein2012mindboggle; @stone2020longitudinal; @stone2024blast; @Marek2011; @smith2013functional], while View 3 comprises eleven neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4` [@rosen1984new], `MMSE` [@folstein1975mini], `CDRSB` [@morris1993clinical], `TRABSCOR` [@reitan1958validity], `FAQ` [@pfeffer1982measurement], and four Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test sub-scores `RAVLT_immediate`, `RAVLT_learning`, `RAVLT_forgetting`, `RAVLT_perc_forgetting` [@rey1964examen]). Following `Protocol B`, the three MRI views align with the cognitive battery during training, but test-set predictions are generated exclusively from structural MRI. In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N = 822$) [@tcga2012breast] and `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$) [@tcga2013kirc], mRNA expression ($p_1 = 200$), somatic copy-number variation ($p_2 = 150$), and RPPA proteomics ($p_3 = 150$) predict clinical Estrogen Receptor status and pathologic tumor stage, respectively.

## Global 12-Dataset Benchmark: Subspace Capacity vs. Single-Axis Interpretability

Across the $B = 12$ dataset blocks and nine architectures, block-averaged non-parametric Friedman [@friedman1937use] and Iman–Davenport [@Iman1980] omnibus tests confirm statistically significant differentiation on both the linear subspace probe ($\chi_F^2 = 31.49, p = 1.15 \times 10^{-4}$; $F_F = 5.37, p = 1.98 \times 10^{-5}$) and the multi-modal consensus probe ($\chi_F^2 = 20.87, p = 0.0075$; $F_F = 3.06, p = 0.0044$, Nemenyi Critical Difference $CD = 3.468$ at $\alpha = 0.05$ [@Demsar2006; @Nemenyi1963; @benavoli2016should]). @tbl-global-leaderboard summarizes the global metrics across all nine models, accompanied by the Demšar Critical Difference diagram (@fig-cd-diagram), the multi-objective speed–accuracy and support–consensus Pareto frontiers (@fig-pareto-frontier), and the three-probe performance profile (@fig-three-probes).

Three empirical principles emerge from @tbl-global-leaderboard and Figures [-@fig-cd-diagram]–[-@fig-three-probes]:

1. **Multi-View Alignment Outperforms Single-Matrix Factorization When Views Differ in Scale or Private Variance**: `LEND` (mean Friedman rank $3.79$), `NED` ($3.88$), `NEDPP` ($3.92$), and `Flow-SiMR-V` ($4.25$) lead the linear entrypoint ranking ahead of concatenated `PCA` ($7.75$) and `NSAFlow-PCA` ($7.67$). On heterogeneous cohorts such as `mfeat` ($p = [76, 64, 6, 47]$) and `Shared+Private` ($p = [160, 60, 30]$), concatenated `PCA` rotates toward the highest-dimensional view (`mfeat` linear accuracy $0.727$, `Shared+Private` $R^2 = 0.618$), whereas cross-view alignment equalizes view contributions (`mfeat` accuracy $0.964$ for `NEDPP` and $0.948$ for `SiMLR-LBFGSB`; `Shared+Private` $R^2 = 0.956$ for `LEND`).
2. **Coordinate-Aligned `nsa_flow` Projections Prevent the Random Forest Axis Drop**: As established in @eq-subspace-invariance, ridge regression on $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ is insensitive to orthogonal or oblique column mixing $\mathbf{V}_m \mathbf{M}$, hiding the fact that dense `PCA` mixes distinct biological mechanisms across columns. When evaluated with coordinate-splitting decision trees (`RandomForest`), `PCA` suffers an average score drop of $\Delta = -0.044$ across the 12 cohorts—collapsing completely on weak sparse factors (`NonnegPartsWeak` linear $R^2 = 0.125 \to$ Random Forest $R^2 = 0.000$) and dropping by $71\%$ on `ADNI-MCI` ($0.152 \to 0.044$). In contrast, `Flow-SiMR-V` ($\Delta = -0.022$) and `LEND` ($\Delta = -0.023$) cut the axis-mixing penalty in half.
3. **Operating Points Match Intrinsic Biological Density ($q = 0.5$ vs. $q = 0.8$)**: @fig-operating-point-and-support demonstrates how the quantile threshold $q$ acts as a tunable lens on feature support recovery. Across the $1,215$-fit operating-point evaluation, moderate sparsity ($q = 0.5$) achieves the highest overall linear predictive score ($0.680$) and highest Random Forest axis score ($0.651$) while recovering $F_1 = 0.989$ (`SiMLR-LBFGSB` on `NonnegParts`) and $F_1 = 0.709$–$1.000$ on $50\%$-sparse ground-truth pathways (`Linear`). When the underlying biology is concentrated in focal $20\%$-active modules (`NonnegPartsWeak` and `Shared+Private`), increasing the quantile threshold to $q = 0.8$ raises support recovery to $F_1 = 0.797$ while preserving $99.1\%$ of peak subspace accuracy ($0.674$ vs. $0.680$).

## Clinical Neuroimaging in `ADNI-MCI` ($N = 1,084$): Predicting Cognitive Decline and Mapping Braak Staging from MRI Alone

A primary clinical test of multi-modal representation learning is whether aligning structural neuroimaging with multi-domain cognitive batteries during training yields an anatomical basis that better predicts cognitive severity in new patients who have only undergone an MRI scan (`Protocol B`). Across $N = 1,084$ participants with Mild Cognitive Impairment, @tbl-adni-mci-summary compares all nine benchmark models on held-out MRI-only prediction of composite cognitive impairment (`CogPC1` $R^2$, after in-fold adjustment for age, sex, and education), single-axis Random Forest prediction, and mean ridge regression $R^2$ across all eleven individual neuropsychological scales (`ADAS11`, `ADAS13`, `ADASQ4`, `MMSE`, `CDRSB`, `TRABSCOR`, `FAQ`, and four `RAVLT` memory scales).

Comparing the unsupervised anatomical baselines against cognitive-aligned SiMR models in @tbl-adni-mci-summary and @fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship yields three core clinical and neurobiological insights:

1. **Supervising MRI Factor Discovery with Cognitive Batteries Improves Out-of-Sample MRI Prediction by $+65.8\%$**: Unsupervised `PCA` on the $382$ structural MRI features explains $R^2 = 0.152 \pm 0.004$ of out-of-sample cognitive variance on the linear probe and collapses to $R^2 = 0.044$ on the single-axis Random Forest probe because its leading component reflects global head and brain size rather than focal neurodegeneration. Aligning the MRI projections against the 11-scale cognitive battery during training raises out-of-sample MRI-only `CogPC1` prediction to $R^2 = 0.252 \pm 0.008$ (`LEND`), $0.231 \pm 0.015$ (`Flow-SiMR-V`, with Random Forest axis $R^2 = 0.197$, a $4.5\times$ improvement over `PCA`), and $0.241$ for linear `SiMLR` solvers in the $1,214$-configuration sweep, while raising mean prediction across all eleven individual cognitive scales by $+32.1\%$ ($R^2 = 0.107$ vs. $0.081$ for `PCA`; peaking on `ADAS13` $R^2 = 0.195$, `ADAS11` $0.165$, and `MMSE` $0.141$).
2. **Orthogonal Varimax Subspace Rotation and Quantile-Sparsified Non-Negative SiMR ($q = 0.85$) Isolate Three Classical Braak Neurofibrillary Networks**: As shown in @fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship, dense `PCA` (Panel A1) assigns nearly uniform negative weights ($\approx -0.15$) across all $62$ DKT cortical thickness parcels on Component 1 ($0\%$ sparsity), mixing temporoparietal association areas with primary motor and visual cortices. Under unrotated PCA initialization without quantile thresholding (Panel A2, `varimax = False, q = None`), Component 1 absorbs this positive global correlation floor across $53/62$ regions ($15\%$ overall sparsity). Enabling default orthogonal Varimax subspace rotation (`varimax = True` in `pysimlr v0.2.17`, Panel A3) rotates the $3$-dimensional subspace before non-negative `nsa_flow` retraction, immediately raising unthresholded sparsity from $15\%$ to $66\%$ with balanced active supports ($[24, 12, 26]$ DKT parcels across $\mathbf{v}_1, \mathbf{v}_2, \mathbf{v}_3$) without requiring manual subject row-mean centering. Combining non-negative `nsa_flow` ($w = 0.50$) with `sparseness = 0.85` (Panels A4 and B) further restricts each latent axis to $9/62$ active DKT regions ($88\%$ overall sparsity, Gram defect $D = 8.2 \times 10^{-5}$) while achieving higher out-of-sample cognitive accuracy ($R^2 = 0.192$) than dense `PCA` ($0.190$):
   * **Component 1 ($\mathbf{v}_1$, Temporoparietal Association Network — Braak Stages IV–V)**: Concentrates weight in `left_middle_temporal` ($+0.670$), `left_supramarginal` ($+0.454$), `right_middle_temporal` ($+0.341$), `right_pars_opercularis` ($+0.319$), and `left_superior_frontal` ($+0.209$). Thinning across these heteromodal temporoparietal and inferior frontal hubs marks the clinical transition from isolated amnestic impairment to language, semantic, and praxis decline [@braak1991neuropathological; @dickerson2009cortical; @buckner2005].
   * **Component 2 ($\mathbf{v}_2$, Medial Temporal Amnestic Core — Braak Stages I–III)**: Isolates bilateral entorhinal cortex (`left_entorhinal` $+0.680$, `right_entorhinal` $+0.226$) and precuneal/cuneal posterior hubs (`right_cuneus` $+0.698$), coupled with subcortical hippocampal volume loss in View 0 (`right_hippocampus` $+0.369$). This circuit directly reflects early transentorhinal tau neurofibrillary pathology responsible for episodic memory encoding failure on `RAVLT` and `ADASQ4` [@braak1991neuropathological; @jack2018nia; @rey1964examen].
   * **Component 3 ($\mathbf{v}_3$, Frontocingulate Salience Network)**: Targets `left_rostral_middle_frontal` ($+0.631$), `right_caudal_anterior_cingulate` ($+0.478$), and bilateral insular cortex (`left_insula` $+0.434$, `right_insula` $+0.429$). Atrophy in this anterior cingulate–insular salience network [@seeley2009neurodegenerative; @menon2010saliency] governs executive set-shifting deficits (`TRABSCOR` [@reitan1958validity]) and everyday functional decline (`FAQ` [@pfeffer1982measurement]).
3. **Spared Primary Sensorimotor Cortex and Support-Shuffled / PCA-Rotated Score Controls Confirm True Anatomical Localization**: Across all three components, primary motor cortex (`right_precentral` $+0.0016$, `left_precentral` $\le 10^{-5}$) and primary somatosensory cortex (`left_postcentral` $\le 10^{-5}$, `right_postcentral` $\le 10^{-5}$) receive effectively zero weight (@fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship B). Because primary sensorimotor neocortex is pathologically spared until end-stage Alzheimer's disease [@braak1991neuropathological; @dickerson2009cortical], its automatic exclusion provides an internal neurobiological control. To further separate coordinate-level axis alignment and anatomical support localization from pure subspace capacity, we evaluate two algorithmic negative controls across all 3 seeds on `ADNI-MCI` (`adni_mci_axis_alignment_controls.csv` via `axis_alignment_control_metrics`): (i) a **PCA-Rotated Score Control** that rotates the learned scores $\mathbf{Z} = [\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m]$ by their in-fold principal-component eigenvectors $\mathbf{Q} \in \mathrm{O}(Mk)$ ($\operatorname{span}(\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{Q}) = \operatorname{span}(\mathbf{Z})$), which leaves the linear probe identically unchanged to machine precision (`Flow-SiMR-V` $0.2403 \to 0.2403$; `LEND` $0.2418 \to 0.2418$; `SiMLR-LBFGSB` $0.1650 \to 0.1650$) while reducing single-axis Random Forest accuracy when localized axes are mixed (`SiMLR-LBFGSB` $0.1123 \to 0.0879$, `LEND` non-negative $0.1617 \to 0.1416$); and (ii) a **Support-Shuffled Basis Control** that permutes the row indices of each $\mathbf{V}_m$ within view $m$ ($\mathbf{V}_m[\pi_m, :]$, preserving exact sparsity, weight magnitudes, and Stiefel orthogonality $\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{V}_m$), which collapses the Random Forest `CogPC1` $R^2$ by $60\%$–$65\%$ (`Flow-SiMR-V` $0.1798 \to 0.0627$, $\Delta = -0.1171$; `LEND` $0.1725 \to 0.0690$, $\Delta = -0.1035$; `NEDPP` $0.1563 \to 0.0668$, $\Delta = -0.0895$) and linear $R^2$ from $0.240$–$0.242$ to $0.151$–$0.157$ (the unstructured `PCA` baseline floor of $0.151$). This confirms that the $+3.8\times$ to $+4.5\times$ Random Forest advantage on `ADNI-MCI` arises directly from localizing true neuroanatomical circuits rather than generic sparsity or basis conditioning.

In `MultiOmics` (`TCGA-BRCA`, $N = 822$), `Flow-SiMR-V`, `LEND`, and `NEDPP` achieve $92.7\% \pm 0.7\%$ out-of-sample Estrogen Receptor classification accuracy (vs. $91.5\%$ for `PCA`), while the sparse non-negative dictionaries $\mathbf{V}_m$ isolate the canonical luminal breast cancer signaling cascade across all three molecular layers (detailed in Appendix A): estrogen receptor alpha (`ER-alpha`) and phosphorylated `ER-alpha_pS118` in RPPA proteomics, master luminal transcription factors `GATA3`, `PGR`, and `ESR1` in mRNA transcriptomics [@perou2000; @parker2009supervised], and focal chromosomal amplifications at `17q23` and `8p11-p12` in somatic copy-number variation [@tcga2012breast; @curtis2012]. In `TCGA-KIRC` ($N = 467$), adding non-linear decoding in `LEND` improves pathologic stage classification on the consensus embedding $\mathbf{U}$ to $71.4\% \pm 0.4\%$ (vs. $67.1\%$ for `PCA`), capturing non-linear metabolic and hypoxia-inducible interactions across transcriptomic and proteomic layers [@tcga2013kirc]. Finally, on compact clinical cohorts (`Diabetes` $R^2 = 0.396$ for `SiMLR-LBFGSB` vs. $0.351$ for `PCA`; `Heart` accuracy $0.848$ for `NSAFlow-PCA`), pairing orthogonal Varimax subspace rotation with `nsa_flow` ($q = 0.50$) cleanly separates each modality into balanced physiological subnetworks (@fig-nsa-v-interpretability)—isolating resting hemodynamics (`trestbps` $0.91$, `restecg` $0.42$) from chest-pain and demographic profile (`cp` $0.70$, `sex` $0.63$, `age` $0.32$) in `Heart` View 1, exercise ST/heart-rate response (`oldpeak` $0.73$, `thalach` $0.50$, `slope` $0.46$) from perfusion/vessel burden (`thal` $0.75$, `exang` $0.57$, `ca` $0.34$) in `Heart` View 2, adiposity/blood pressure (`bp` $0.73$, `bmi` $0.68$) from age/sex (`age` $0.78$, `sex` $0.62$) in `Diabetes` View 1, and the glycemic/triglyceride triad (`s5` $0.63$, `s6` $0.56$, `s4` $0.54$) from lipoprotein cholesterol (`s2` $0.71$, `s1` $0.70$) in `Diabetes` View 2—while the linear entrypoint $\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ decomposes any individual patient's risk score into exact feature-level clinical contributions $c_{m,i,j,l} = x_{m,i,j} v_{m,j,l}$ without post-hoc Monte Carlo approximations [@Wachter_2017; @karimi2021algorithmic; @pearl2009causality] (@fig-multiomics-and-patient-attribution B and @fig-heart-audit). Complete parameter sensitivity ablations—including the $w \in [0.01, 0.95]$ trade-off curve, row-mean/ICA preprocessing controls, latent rank $k \in \{2, 3, 5, 8\}$ scaling, and pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum tests—are provided in Appendix B.
